separable: separable — *use up the last of the milk*, *use the last of the milk up*; a pronoun must sit in the middle: *use it up*, never ✗ *use up it*
gloss: To consume all of something so that none of it is left.
examples: Don't *use up* all the hot water — I still need a shower.
The kids *used* the last of the printer paper *up* on Monday.
We're *using up* the leftovers before the trip.
contrast: The verb is voiced: *use* /juːz/, *used up* /juːzd/. The noun *use* and the *used to* of past habit both take /s/: /juːs/, /juːst/.

separable: separable, and it normally splits — the person or animal sits in the middle: *the crowd urged her on*; *urge on the runners* is possible but bookish, and a pronoun can never follow: ✗ *urged on her*
gloss: To encourage someone to keep going or to try harder.
examples: The crowd *urged* her *on* down the final stretch.
His coach has *urged* him *on* since he was nine.
Parents lined the course, *urging on* the smallest runners.

separable: separable — *usher in a new era*, *usher a new era in*; in practice it rarely splits, but a pronoun goes in the middle: *usher it in*, never ✗ *usher in it*
gloss: To mark or bring about the beginning of a new period.
examples: One ruling like that can *usher in* years of litigation.
The 2008 crash *ushered in* a decade of caution.
Cheap sensors are *ushering in* a new kind of farming.

separable: separable — *usher out the old system*, *usher the old system out*, *usher it out*; never ✗ *usher out it*
gloss: To mark the end of a period, or to move something aside as it ends.
examples: The ceremony *ushers out* the old year at midnight.
That election *ushered out* forty years of one-party rule.
The company is quietly *ushering out* its paper forms.

separable: inseparable — the person on the receiving end follows *on*: *unload on the refs*, *unload on him*, never ✗ *unload him on*
gloss: To let out all your anger at someone in a rush of criticism.
examples: The coach *unloaded on* the referee after the call.
Don't *unload on* the intern — it wasn't her decision.
He's been *unloading on* everyone in the office all week.

separable: the thing you are getting rid of goes straight after the verb and the person after *on*: *unload the old van on his nephew*, *unload it on me*; ✗ *unload on his nephew the old van*
gloss: To get rid of something you don't want by passing or selling it to someone else.
examples: He *unloaded* his old minivan *on* his nephew.
They're trying to *unload* the unsold units *on* small investors.
She's *unloading* her old textbooks *on* anyone who'll take them.

ru: избирать, избрать (на должность); проводить, провести (на выборах)
separable: separable — *vote in a new mayor*, *vote the new mayor in*; a pronoun must split it: *vote them in*, never ✗ *vote in them*
gloss: To elect someone to a position by voting for them.
examples: They *voted* her *in* by a twenty-point margin.
If he won't budge, we'll *vote in* somebody who will.
The board has *voted in* a new chair.

ru: смещать, сместить (голосованием); не переизбирать, не переизбрать
separable: separable — *vote out the incumbent*, *vote the incumbent out*, *vote him out*; never ✗ *vote out him*
gloss: To remove someone from office by voting against them at an election.
examples: Voters *voted* the mayor *out* after a single term.
Two senators were *voted out* last November.
They're threatening to *vote* the whole council *out*.

separable: separable — *vote off the loudest player*, *vote him off*; a pronoun has to split it: *voted her off*, never ✗ *voted off her*. Very often passive: *he got voted off*
gloss: To force someone out of a contest or a show by voting against them.
examples: They *vote* one contestant *off* every Thursday.
The audience *voted* him *off* in week three.
She's terrified of being *voted off* before the finale.

separable: separable — *vote down the amendment*, *vote the amendment down*, *vote it down*; never ✗ *vote down it*
gloss: To reject a proposal by voting against it.
examples: The council *voted down* the parking plan 7–2.
The measure has been *voted down* twice already.
If they *vote* it *down* again, the project dies.

separable: separable — *vote through the budget*, *vote the budget through*, *vote it through*; never ✗ *vote through it*
gloss: To approve something officially by voting for it.
examples: The committee *voted through* a watered-down version of the bill.
If they *vote* it *through* tonight, it takes effect in January.
The raise was *voted through* without a word of debate.
contrast: Americans usually say a bill was *passed*; *vote through* points at the vote itself as the thing that pushed it past the last hurdle.

ru: голосовать, проголосовать (по вопросу); ставить, поставить на голосование
separable: inseparable — the question being decided follows *on*: *vote on the proposal*, *vote on it*, never ✗ *vote it on*
gloss: To settle a question by holding a vote about it.
examples: The board *votes on* the merger Thursday.
We *voted on* three different logos before anyone agreed.
They're still *voting on* whether to reopen the pool.
contrast: Three prepositions, three jobs: you *vote on* the question, *vote for* the candidate you want, and *vote against* the one you don't.

separable: no object of its own — *the truck veered off*; when a road follows, *off* takes it and nothing can come between: *veered off the highway*, never ✗ *veered the highway off*
gloss: To turn suddenly to one side, leaving the course you were on.
examples: The truck *veered off* and clipped a guardrail.
A car had *veered off* the road in the ice.
Watch the front wheel — it keeps *veering off* to the left.

ru: отклоняться, отклониться (от темы); уходить, уйти в сторону
separable: no object — *the meeting veered off again*; a topic follows *off* directly: *veered off topic*, *veered off course*
gloss: To drift away from the subject or the plan you were following.
examples: Every meeting *veers off* into office gossip.
He *veered off* topic about ten minutes in.
The project had *veered* badly *off* course by March.

ru: выбираться, выбраться (наружу); отваживаться выйти, отважиться выйти
separable: no object — nothing goes between the two words: *venture out into the storm*, never ✗ *venture the storm out*
gloss: To go outside or leave a safe place when doing so takes some nerve.
examples: Nobody *ventured out* during the blizzard.
She rarely *ventures out* after dark.
We're *venturing out* for groceries once the rain stops.

ru: браться, взяться (за новое дело); пробовать себя, попробовать себя (в новой области)
separable: inseparable — the new field follows *into*: *venture into politics*, *venture into it*, never ✗ *venture it into*
gloss: To start doing something new and risky, especially a new line of business.
examples: The studio *ventured into* video games and lost a fortune.
Few small banks *venture into* crypto lending.
He's *venturing into* real estate at sixty.

separable: inseparable — the person follows *with*: *visit with your aunt*, *visit with her*, never ✗ *visit her with*
gloss: To spend a while sitting and talking with someone.
examples: We *visited with* the neighbors on the porch for an hour.
Come sit down and *visit with* us a while.
She's in the kitchen, *visiting with* my mother.
contrast: *Visit* someone means go and see them; *visit with* someone means sit and talk, even in your own house. The *with* version is American — a British speaker would say *chat to*.

ru: бездельничать, побездельничать; отдыхать, отдохнуть (ничего не делая)
separable: no object — *veg out on the couch*; nothing can come between the two words
gloss: To do nothing at all for a while, usually in front of a screen.
examples: I just want to *veg out* in front of the TV tonight.
We *vegged out* all Sunday and regretted nothing.
He's been *vegging out* since finals ended.
contrast: Short for *vegetate*: the *g* is soft — VEJ — and it doubles before an ending, *vegged*, *vegging*.
